description: File audited financial statements with ROC within 30 days of AGM
obligation_register: Failure to file financial statements: company liable to penalty of Rs 10,000 plus Rs 1,000/day of continuing default (max Rs 2,00,000); officers in default (MD/CFO, or the director charged with responsibility, else all directors) liable to Rs 10,000 plus Rs 100/day (max Rs 50,000). Liable: company and officer(s) in default. Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.137(3). [Search-confirmed - taxguru.in, ca2013.com]

description: File annual return within 60 days of AGM; MGT-7A for OPC and small companies
acts_rules: Companies Act 2013 s.92; Companies (Management and Administration) Rules 2014
obligation_register: Failure to file annual return: company and every officer in default liable to penalty of Rs 10,000 plus Rs 100/day of continuing default (max Rs 2,00,000 for company, Rs 50,000 for officer); 3 consecutive years of AOC-4/MGT-7 default also trigger director disqualification. Liable: company and officer in default. Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.92(5). [Search-confirmed - taxguru.in, legalsuvidha.com]

description: Intimate ROC of auditor appointment within 15 days of AGM/board appointment
acts_rules: Companies Act 2013 s.139; Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules 2014
obligation_register: No filing-specific penalty is prescribed for ADT-1; default in complying with auditor appointment/intimation provisions falls under the residual penalty - company and every officer in default liable to Rs 10,000 plus Rs 1,000/day (max Rs 2,00,000 for company, Rs 50,000 for officer). Liable: company and officer in default. Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.450 (general penalty), read with s.139. [Knowledge-based]

description: Every DIN holder to file KYC annually
frequency_or_trigger: Annual; due date 30 September unless MCA notifies otherwise
acts_rules: Companies (Appointment and Qualification of Directors) Rules 2014 r.12A
verification: Knowledge-based - due date/web-form option to be checked per current MCA circular
obligation_register: DIN is marked 'Deactivated due to non-filing of DIR-3 KYC' and remains deactivated until KYC is filed with a late fee of Rs 5,000; a deactivated DIN holder cannot sign MCA e-forms or be appointed as director elsewhere. Liable: director (DIN holder) personally. Basis: Companies (Appointment and Qualification of Directors) Rules 2014 r.12A. [Search-confirmed - treelife.in, caclubindia.com]

description: Return of deposits and particulars of money received not being deposits
acts_rules: Companies Act 2013 s.73; Companies (Acceptance of Deposits) Rules 2014 r.16
obligation_register: Contravention of deposit acceptance/repayment norms: company liable to fine of not less than Rs 1 crore up to Rs 10 crore; every officer in default liable to imprisonment up to 7 years and fine not less than Rs 25 lakh up to Rs 2 crore. Liable: company and officer in default (imprisonment risk). Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.76A (read with s.73). [Search-confirmed - taxguru.in, ca2013.com]

compliance_name: Half-yearly MSME payment outstanding return (MSME Form I)
description: Report dues to micro/small suppliers outstanding over 45 days
frequency_or_trigger: Half-yearly (April-September by 31 Oct; October-March by 30 Apr)
acts_rules: MCA Order dated 22 Jan 2019 under s.405 Companies Act 2013
obligation_register: Failure to file MSME Form I / furnishing incorrect information: company liable to fine up to Rs 25,000; officers in default (director/CS/CFO) liable to imprisonment up to 6 months or fine of Rs 25,000-3,00,000, or both. Liable: company and officers in default. Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.405(4). [Search-confirmed - taxguru.in, vjmglobal.com]

description: Report CSR spend as addendum to financial statements filing
acts_rules: Companies (CSR Policy) Rules 2014; Companies Act 2013 s.135
obligation_register: Same non-compliance/penalty regime as CSR spend default under s.135(7) applies where CSR-2 disclosure/spend obligations are not met - company liable to penalty of twice the unspent amount or Rs 1 crore, whichever is less; every officer in default liable to one-tenth of the unspent amount or Rs 2 lakh, whichever is less. Liable: company and officer in default. Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.135(7). [Search-confirmed - cleartax.in, taxmann.com]

description: Constitute CSR committee (where spend above Rs50 lakh), spend 2% of average net profit, transfer unspent amount to specified fund/account
frequency_or_trigger: Annual; unspent to Unspent CSR A/c within 30 days of FY end; ongoing project amount within 3 years
form_or_filing: Board report annexure; Form CSR-1 for implementing agencies
acts_rules: Companies Act 2013 s.135, Sch VII; CSR Rules 2014
obligation_register: Failure to spend/transfer CSR amount: company liable to penalty of twice the amount required to be transferred or Rs 1 crore, whichever is less; every officer in default liable to one-tenth of that amount or Rs 2 lakh, whichever is less. Liable: company and officer in default. Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.135(7). [Search-confirmed - cleartax.in, taxmann.com]

description: Implementing agencies to register to receive CSR funds
obligation_register: No specific penalty is prescribed for CSR-1 non-registration itself; an unregistered implementing agency cannot receive CSR funds (spend is disallowed), and any consequential CSR-spend shortfall is penalised under s.135(7). General default otherwise falls under the residual penalty for company/officer in default. Liable: company and officer in default. Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.135(7)/s.450. [Knowledge-based]

compliance_name: Register of beneficial owners / SBO declaration (BEN-2)
description: Significant beneficial owner files BEN-1 with company; company files BEN-2 within 30 days
frequency_or_trigger: Within 30 days of receipt of BEN-1
obligation_register: Failure of SBO to declare: penalty of Rs 50,000 plus Rs 1,000/day (max Rs 2,00,000); company's failure to maintain register/file BEN-2 or denying inspection: penalty of Rs 1,00,000 plus Rs 500/day (max Rs 5,00,000); officers in default: Rs 25,000 plus Rs 200/day (max Rs 1,00,000); wilful false declaration is prosecuted under s.447 (fraud). Liable: SBO, company, and officer in default. Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.90(10)/(11). [Search-confirmed - ssrana.in, mondaq.com]

compliance_name: Notice to members on SBO (MGT-4/5 / s.90 notices)
description: Company to seek declarations from persons suspected to hold significant beneficial interest
obligation_register: Same tiered penalty structure as SBO declaration failure applies to non-issuance/non-response to s.90 notices - member/SBO liable to Rs 50,000 plus Rs 1,000/day (max Rs 2,00,000); company/officer in default liable as under s.90(10)-(11). Liable: member/SBO, company and officer in default. Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.90. [Search-confirmed - ssrana.in, mondaq.com]

description: Declaration of commencement of business within 180 days of incorporation and before commencing business
obligation_register: Failure to file INC-20A / commence business: company liable to penalty of Rs 50,000; every officer in default liable to Rs 1,000/day of continuing default, max Rs 1,00,000; continued non-compliance can also lead to ROC striking off the company's name. Liable: company and officer in default. Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.10A(2). [Search-confirmed - taxguru.in, corpbiz.io]

description: Maintain registered office; file notice of situation and changes
frequency_or_trigger: Within 30 days of incorporation; on change
obligation_register: Default in registered-office compliance (verification/display/change intimation): company and every officer in default liable to penalty of Rs 1,000 per day of default, subject to a maximum of Rs 1,00,000. Liable: company and officer in default. Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.12(8). [Search-confirmed - mbgcorp.com, ca2013.com]

description: Hold at least 4 board meetings, gap not exceeding 120 days
obligation_register: Officer whose duty is to give notice of a board meeting and fails to do so is liable to a penalty of Rs 25,000; persistent failure to hold the minimum number of board meetings is also treated as a governance lapse examined by ROC/adjudicating officers. Liable: officer responsible for giving notice (not automatically all directors). Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.173(4). [Search-confirmed - ca2013.com, taxtmi.com]

description: Hold AGM within 6 months of FY end; gap not exceeding 15 months
frequency_or_trigger: By 30 September (extension via ROC s.96 application)
form_or_filing: AGM notice; minutes; MGT-14 where special resolution
obligation_register: Default in holding AGM: company and every officer in default punishable with fine up to Rs 1,00,000, and in case of continuing default, further fine up to Rs 5,000 per day of default. Liable: company and officer in default. Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.99 (for default under s.96). [Search-confirmed - ca2013.com, taxtmi.com]

description: Comply with ICSI Secretarial Standards on board and general meetings
acts_rules: Companies Act 2013 s.118, s.205 ; SS-1; SS-2
obligation_register: SS-1/SS-2 are mandatory Secretarial Standards under s.118(10); no separate fine is fixed for SS non-compliance per se, but resulting defects in minutes/notices attract the s.118(11) penalty (Rs 25,000 on company, Rs 5,000 on officer in default) and can taint related filings (MGT-14/board reports). Liable: company and officer in default. Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.118(11). [Knowledge-based]

description: File special resolutions and specified board resolutions with ROC
obligation_register: Default in filing resolutions/agreements: company liable to penalty of Rs 10,000 plus Rs 100/day (subject to caps applied in practice up to Rs 2,00,000 for company / Rs 50,000 for officer/director in default); adjudication orders have imposed amounts up to these caps. Liable: company and every officer in default. Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.117(2). [Search-confirmed - taxguru.in, icsi.edu]

description: Maintain registers of members, directors/KMP, charges, contracts (s.189), loans and investments, etc.
form_or_filing: Statutory registers (MGT-1, MBP-2, MBP-3 etc. formats)
obligation_register: Failure to maintain statutory registers (members, charges, loans/investments, contracts) attracts the specific penalty under the relevant section (e.g. s.88(5) Rs 3,00,000 company / Rs 50,000 officer for register of members); where no specific amount is fixed, the residual penalty applies. Liable: company and officer in default. Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.88(5) and s.450 (residual). [Knowledge-based]

compliance_name: Related party transactions approval and disclosure
description: Board/shareholder approval for RPT; disclose in AOC-2 in board report
form_or_filing: Form AOC-2; MBP-4 (Reg. of contracts s.189)
acts_rules: Companies Act 2013 s.188; Companies (Meetings of Board) Rules 2014 r.15
obligation_register: Contract entered without board/shareholder approval under s.188: director/employee who authorised it is liable, for listed companies to a penalty of Rs 25 lakh, and for other companies Rs 5 lakh; the transaction is voidable at the company's option and the person concerned must indemnify the company for any loss. Liable: director/employee who authorised the contract. Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.188(5). [Search-confirmed - ipleaders blog.ipleaders.in, ibclaw.in]

description: Comply with limits and approvals; file MGT-14 where special resolution
obligation_register: Contravention of loan/investment/guarantee limits under s.186: company liable to penalty of not less than Rs 25,000 up to Rs 5,00,000; every officer in default liable to imprisonment up to 2 years and fine not less than Rs 25,000 up to Rs 1,00,000. Liable: company and officer in default (imprisonment risk for officer). Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.186(13). [Search-confirmed - 5paisa.com, cleartax.in]

compliance_name: Directors' disclosure of interest (MBP-1) and DIR-8
description: Annual disclosure of interest and non-disqualification declaration
frequency_or_trigger: First board meeting of each FY; on appointment
obligation_register: Failure of a director to disclose interest (MBP-1) or file DIR-8: director liable to imprisonment up to 1 year or fine of Rs 1,00,000 to Rs 5,00,000, or both, and the contract may be voidable; concealment can also lead to vacation of office under s.167. Liable: director personally. Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.184(4). [Knowledge-based]

description: File particulars of appointment/cessation of directors and KMP
obligation_register: Default in filing particulars of director/KMP appointment (DIR-12): company and officer in default liable to penalty of Rs 10,000 plus Rs 1,000/day of continuing default (max Rs 2,00,000 for company / Rs 50,000 for officer), applying the residual penalty regime since no bespoke amount is fixed for DIR-12 filing. Liable: company and officer in default. Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.450. [Knowledge-based]

description: Company and director filing on resignation
frequency_or_trigger: DIR-11 by resigning director (optional); DIR-12 by company within 30 days
obligation_register: Failure to file director resignation particulars: company liable to penalty of Rs 10,000 plus Rs 1,000/day (max Rs 2,00,000); officer in default liable to Rs 10,000 plus Rs 1,000/day (max Rs 50,000), under the residual penalty since s.168 itself has no bespoke fine for the filing default. Liable: company and officer in default. Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.450. [Knowledge-based]

description: Prepare board report with prescribed disclosures
obligation_register: Non-compliance with Board's report requirements: company liable to penalty of Rs 3,00,000 and every officer in default liable to Rs 50,000. Liable: company and officer in default. Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.134(8). [Search-confirmed - taxguru.in, ca2013.com]

description: Independent director databank registration and proficiency test; appointment norms
acts_rules: Companies Act 2013 s.149; Companies (Appointment and Qualification of Directors) Rules 2014 r.6
obligation_register: Non-appointment of required independent directors / non-empanelment in the databank: treated as a residual default - company and officer in default liable to penalty of Rs 10,000 plus Rs 1,000/day (max Rs 2,00,000 for company / Rs 50,000 for officer/director). Liable: company and officer in default. Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.450 (read with s.149). [Knowledge-based]

description: Appoint at least one woman director on board where thresholds met
obligation_register: Non-compliance with the mandatory woman-director requirement is enforced through the general penalty provision - company and every officer in default liable to Rs 10,000 plus Rs 1,000/day of default (max Rs 2,00,000 for company / Rs 50,000 for officer). Liable: company and officer in default. Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.450 (read with s.149(1)). [Knowledge-based]

description: At least one director resident in India for 182 days
obligation_register: Non-compliance with the resident-director requirement (director staying in India >=182 days) is enforced through the general penalty provision - company and every officer in default liable to Rs 10,000 plus Rs 1,000/day of default (max Rs 2,00,000 for company / Rs 50,000 for officer). Liable: company and officer in default. Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.450 (read with s.149(3)). [Knowledge-based]

description: Secretarial audit report for listed and large companies
obligation_register: Company/officer/CS-in-practice contravening secretarial audit requirements (MR-3) liable to a penalty of Rs 2,00,000 (this replaced the earlier fine of Rs 1,00,000-5,00,000 with effect from 21 Dec 2020). Liable: company, officer in default, or the practising Company Secretary. Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.204(4). [Search-confirmed - ca2013.com, taxguru.in]

compliance_name: Cost audit and CRA filings (CRA-2, CRA-4)
description: Appointment of cost auditor and filing of cost audit report where cost records applicable
frequency_or_trigger: Annual; CRA-4 within 30 days of receipt of report
acts_rules: Companies Act 2013 s.148; Cost Records Rules 2014
obligation_register: Default in cost-audit compliance: company and officer in default punishable as under s.147(1) - fine of Rs 25,000 to Rs 5,00,000 for the company, and imprisonment up to 1 year or fine of Rs 10,000 to Rs 1,00,000 for officer in default; the cost auditor in default is punishable under s.147(2)-(4). Liable: company, officer in default, and cost auditor. Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.148(8) read with s.147. [Search-confirmed - taxguru.in, ibclaw.in]

description: Appointment of internal auditor for prescribed companies
obligation_register: Failure to appoint an internal auditor where mandated is enforced through the residual penalty - company and officer in default liable to Rs 10,000 plus Rs 1,000/day of default (max Rs 2,00,000 for company / Rs 50,000 for officer). Liable: company and officer in default. Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.450 (read with s.138). [Knowledge-based]

description: Constitute committees for listed and prescribed public companies
obligation_register: Non-constitution of Audit Committee/NRC where mandated: company liable to penalty of Rs 5,00,000, and every officer in default liable to Rs 1,00,000 (audit committee, s.178(8) applies the same quantum to NRC non-compliance). Liable: company and officer in default. Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.178(8) (Audit Committee provisions under s.177 carry a parallel penalty). [Knowledge-based]

description: Establish vigil mechanism for prescribed companies
obligation_register: Non-establishment or non-operation of the vigil mechanism is penalised in the same manner as other Audit Committee defaults - company liable to Rs 5,00,000 and officer in default liable to Rs 1,00,000. Liable: company and officer in default. Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.178(8) (read with s.177(9)). [Knowledge-based]

frequency_or_trigger: Within 30 days (extendable to 300 days with fee)
obligation_register: Default in registering a charge (CHG-1/CHG-9): company liable to penalty of Rs 5,00,000 and every officer in default liable to Rs 50,000; wilful furnishing of false/incorrect particulars is punishable under s.447 (fraud). Liable: company and officer in default. Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.86. [Search-confirmed - ca2013.com, ibclaw.in]

description: File satisfaction of charge with ROC
obligation_register: Default in filing satisfaction of charge (CHG-4) is punished under the same charges-chapter penalty - company liable to Rs 5,00,000 and every officer in default liable to Rs 50,000. Liable: company and officer in default. Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.86 (Chapter VI penalty, applicable to s.82 default). [Search-confirmed - ca2013.com, ibclaw.in]

description: File return of allotment of shares
obligation_register: Default in filing return of allotment (PAS-3): company and officer in default liable to a penalty of Rs 1,000 for each day of default, or Rs 1,00,000, whichever is less, for each default. Liable: company and officer in default. Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.39(4). [Search-confirmed - taxguru.in, ca2013.com]

description: Private placement offer letter and reconciliation of share capital audit
frequency_or_trigger: Per offer; PAS-6 half-yearly for unlisted public companies
acts_rules: Companies Act 2013 s.42; Companies (Prospectus and Allotment of Securities) Rules 2014
obligation_register: Contravention of private placement provisions (PAS-4/5/6): company, its promoters and directors liable to a penalty which may extend to the amount raised through the private placement or Rs 2 crore, whichever is lower; the company must also refund all money with interest within 30 days of the order. Liable: company, promoters and directors. Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.42(10). [Search-confirmed - ipleaders, ca2013.com]

description: Unlisted public companies to issue and hold securities in demat form; other companies per rules
acts_rules: Companies (Prospectus and Allotment of Securities) Second Amendment Rules 2018; Companies (Share Capital and Debentures) Rules
verification: Knowledge-based - private-company demat applicability changed in 2023-24; Needs verification
obligation_register: Non-dematerialisation of securities where mandated by the Prospectus/Allotment Rules is enforced through the residual penalty applicable to Companies (Prospectus and Allotment of Securities) Rules contraventions - company and officer in default liable to Rs 10,000 plus Rs 1,000/day (max Rs 2,00,000 for company / Rs 50,000 for officer); non-compliant allotments/transfers can also be restrained. Liable: company and officer in default. Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.450. [Knowledge-based]

compliance_name: Filing of DIR-3 KYC for new DINs (DIR-3)
acts_rules: Companies (Appointment and Qualification of Directors) Rules 2014
obligation_register: Same DIN deactivation and Rs 5,000 late-fee consequence as DIR-3 KYC applies to newly-allotted DINs that miss the KYC deadline. Liable: director (DIN holder) personally. Basis: Companies (Appointment and Qualification of Directors) Rules 2014 r.12A. [Search-confirmed - treelife.in, caclubindia.com]

description: Furnish particulars of company and registered office for active company tag
verification: Knowledge-based - due dates Needs manual check
obligation_register: Non-filing of INC-22A (ACTIVE): company is marked 'ACTIVE-non-compliant' on the MCA master data (blocking key filings such as DIR-12, SH-7, PAS-3, INC-22, INC-28) and can file only on payment of a late fee of Rs 10,000. Liable: company (filing restrictions); officers in default may also face residual penalty under s.450 for continued non-compliance. Basis: Companies (Incorporation) Rules 2014 r.25A; Companies Act 2013 s.450. [Knowledge-based]

description: Auditor reports on accounts under CARO 2020
obligation_register: CARO itself imposes no direct penalty on the company; if the statutory auditor fails to report as required by the Order, the auditor faces the penal consequences of s.147(2)-(4) (fine and, for fraud, prosecution under s.447), and the company's officers may face residual liability if information is withheld from the auditor. Liable: statutory auditor primarily; company/officers if information withheld. Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.147(2)-(4) (Companies (Auditor's Report) Order 2020). [Knowledge-based]

description: Auditor resigning to file ADT-3 within 30 days
obligation_register: Contravention of auditor-resignation intimation requirements (ADT-3): auditor punishable with fine of not less than Rs 50,000 up to Rs 5,00,000. Liable: the outgoing auditor personally. Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.140(3). [Search-confirmed - ca2013.com, taxtmi.com]

compliance_name: Removal of name / strike-off (STK-2) and dormant company
description: Application for strike-off of defunct company; dormant company status
frequency_or_trigger: When defunct; dormant status form MSC-1
obligation_register: Fraudulent or improper application for strike-off (STK-2) is punishable under s.448/s.447 (fraud) and directors of a struck-off company remain liable for outstanding liabilities; dormant-company non-compliance is dealt with under s.455(5) (ROC striking the name off the register of dormant companies). Liable: company and directors. Basis: Companies Act 2013 ss.248, 455(5), 447. [Search-confirmed - taxguru.in, indiankanoon.org]

description: Dormant companies to file annual return
frequency_or_trigger: Annual within 30 days of FY end
obligation_register: Failure of a dormant company to comply with the minimal filing/financial requirements of s.455 leads to the Registrar striking its name off the register of dormant companies (and, in effect, off the register of companies), after following the s.248 process. Liable: company (loss of dormant/company status); directors face residual liability for pre-strike-off defaults. Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.455(5). [Search-confirmed - indiankanoon.org, ibclaw.in]

compliance_name: Reservation of name and change of name (RUN, INC-24)
description: Name approval and change of name
obligation_register: Default in the name-reservation/name-change process (RUN, INC-24) is enforced through the residual penalty - company and officer in default liable to Rs 10,000 plus Rs 1,000/day (max Rs 2,00,000 for company / Rs 50,000 for officer); a reserved name that lapses without incorporation/change simply becomes unavailable, with no separate fine. Liable: company and officer in default. Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.450 (read with s.13). [Knowledge-based]

description: Amend memorandum/articles; increase in authorised capital
form_or_filing: SH-7; MGT-14; INC-28 where NCLT order
obligation_register: Default in filing/effecting an alteration of MOA/AOA (INC-24, MGT-14, SH-7) attracts, for the MGT-14 leg, the s.117(2) penalty (company/officer up to Rs 2,00,000/Rs 50,000 in practice); for other filing defaults the residual s.450 penalty applies. Liable: company and officer in default. Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.117(2)/s.450. [Knowledge-based]

Failure to file NCLT/court orders (e.g. INC-28) with the Registrar is enforced through the residual penalty - company and officer in default liable to Rs 10,000 plus Rs 1,000/day (max Rs 2,00,000 for company / Rs 50,000 for officer); non-filing can also render the order/scheme ineffective against third parties. Liable: company and officer in default. Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.450. [Knowledge-based]

compliance_name: Investor Education and Protection Fund transfers (IEPF-1, IEPF-2)
description: Transfer unpaid/unclaimed dividends and shares to IEPF
frequency_or_trigger: After 7 years of unpaid dividend; statement in IEPF-2
obligation_register: Failure to transfer unclaimed dividends/shares to the IEPF within the prescribed time: company and every officer in default liable to a penalty of Rs 1 lakh, and in case of continuing failure, a further penalty of Rs 500 per day (subject to a maximum of Rs 10 lakh for the company/Rs 2 lakh for the officer, as fixed by the amended provision). Liable: company and officer in default. Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.124(7). [Knowledge-based]

description: Appoint whole-time CS for prescribed companies
obligation_register: Non-appointment of a whole-time Company Secretary where mandated (paid-up capital Rs 10 crore+): company liable to a penalty of Rs 5 lakh; every director and KMP in default liable to Rs 50,000 plus Rs 1,000/day of continuing default (max Rs 5 lakh). Liable: company, directors and KMP in default. Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.203(5). [Search-confirmed - taxguru.in, compliancecalendar.in]

compliance_name: Compliance certificate / audit for paid-up capital of Rs10cr+
description: Whole-time CS for companies with paid-up capital Rs10cr+
acts_rules: Companies (Appointment and Remuneration of Managerial Personnel) Rules 2014 r.8A
obligation_register: Failure to obtain/file the compliance certificate for companies without a whole-time CS (paid-up capital Rs 10 crore+) is treated as a filing default under s.203, exposing the company to the s.203(5) penalty (company Rs 5 lakh; director/KMP Rs 50,000 plus Rs 1,000/day, max Rs 5 lakh). Liable: company, directors and KMP in default. Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.203(5) read with r.8A of the Managerial Personnel Rules 2014. [Knowledge-based]

description: Appointment of MD/WTD and remuneration within s.197 limits
obligation_register: Contravention of the managerial-remuneration limits/procedure under s.197: the person contravening is punishable with a fine of not less than Rs 1 lakh, extending to Rs 5 lakh; any excess remuneration drawn must be refunded to the company, and the company cannot waive recovery without Central Government approval. Liable: the managerial person/director drawing excess remuneration. Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.197(15). [Search-confirmed - indiankanoon.org, taxtmi.com]

description: Respond to notices and compound offences
obligation_register: Section 441 itself is the compounding mechanism (offences punishable only with fine, or fine or imprisonment, may be compounded by the Regional Director/NCLT on payment of a compounding sum); disqualification of directors for repeated defaults is separately dealt with under s.164(2)/s.167, and non-compounded offences proceed to adjudication under s.454/prosecution. Liable: company, officer in default, or the director being disqualified. Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.441 (compounding) read with ss.164(2), 454. [Knowledge-based]

frequency_or_trigger: Within 60 days of FY end (30 May)
obligation_register: Failure to file Form 11 (annual return): LLP and its designated partners liable to a penalty of Rs 100 per day of default, subject to a maximum of Rs 1,00,000 for the LLP and Rs 50,000 for each designated partner. Liable: LLP and designated partners. Basis: LLP Act 2008 s.35(2)/(3) (as substituted, LLP (Amendment) Act 2021). [Search-confirmed - taxguru.in, indiafilings.com]

compliance_name: LLP Statement of Account and Solvency (Form 8)
description: File statement of account and solvency
frequency_or_trigger: Within 30 days from end of 6 months of FY (30 Oct)
obligation_register: Failure to file Form 8 (Statement of Account & Solvency): LLP and designated partners liable to a penalty of Rs 100 per day of default, subject to a maximum of Rs 1,00,000 for the LLP and Rs 50,000 for each designated partner. Liable: LLP and designated partners. Basis: LLP Act 2008 s.34(4) (as substituted). [Search-confirmed - indiankanoon.org, ibclaw.in]

description: Notice of change of partners/designated partners
obligation_register: Default in filing changes of partners/designated partners (Form 4): LLP and every designated partner punishable with a fine of not less than Rs 2,000 up to Rs 25,000; a partner who fails to inform a change is separately punishable with a fine of Rs 2,000 to Rs 25,000. Liable: LLP, designated partners, and the partner concerned. Basis: LLP Act 2008 s.25(6). [Search-confirmed - indiankanoon.org, ibclaw.in]

Same DIN/DPIN deactivation and Rs 5,000 late-fee consequence as company-director DIR-3 KYC applies to designated partners holding a DPIN. Liable: designated partner (DPIN holder) personally. Basis: LLP Rules 2009 (applying Companies (Appointment and Qualification of Directors) Rules 2014 r.12A by reference). [Search-confirmed - treelife.in, caclubindia.com]

description: LLP agreement changes and registered office change
obligation_register: Default in filing change of registered office/other particulars (Form 3/5): LLP and every designated partner punishable with a fine of not less than Rs 2,000 up to Rs 25,000, consistent with the general LLP Act penalty pattern for particulars filings. Liable: LLP and designated partners. Basis: LLP Act 2008 ss.13, 14 (read with the general default-filing fine structure under s.25/parallel provisions). [Knowledge-based]

description: Audit where contribution exceeds Rs25 lakh or turnover exceeds Rs40 lakh
acts_rules: LLP Act 2008 s.34; LLP Rules 2009 r.24
obligation_register: Failure to maintain books of account/get accounts audited as required: LLP liable to a fine of Rs 25,000 to Rs 5,00,000; every designated partner liable to a fine of Rs 10,000 to Rs 1,00,000 (in addition to the Rs 100/day Form 8 filing default penalty under s.34(4)). Liable: LLP and designated partners. Basis: LLP Act 2008 s.34(3)/r.24, LLP Rules 2009. [Search-confirmed - indiankanoon.org, indiafilings.com]

Beneficial-ownership disclosure obligations were extended to LLPs by the LLP (Amendment) Rules aligning with Companies Act SBO norms; non-declaration/non-maintenance is expected to attract a penalty structure comparable to s.90 SBO defaults (fine on the LLP/designated partner and on the person failing to declare), though the LLP-specific quantum has not been independently confirmed for this register. Liable: partner/beneficial owner and LLP/designated partner. Basis: LLP (Amendment) Act 2021 provisions on significant beneficial ownership - Penalty provision not independently confirmed - consult a company secretary/legal counsel. [Needs manual check]

compliance_name: Section 8 licence conditions and annual compliance
description: Comply with licence conditions; annual filings similar to companies; no dividend to members
acts_rules: Companies Act 2013 s.8; Companies (Incorporation) Rules 2014 r.19
obligation_register: Contravention of s.8 licence conditions (using profits for objects other than promotion of the specified objects, or paying dividend): Central Government may revoke the s.8 licence, and if the affairs were conducted fraudulently, every officer in default is punishable under s.447; otherwise the company is liable to a fine of Rs 10 lakh to Rs 1 crore and every officer in default to imprisonment up to 3 years or fine of Rs 25,000 to Rs 25 lakh, or both. Liable: company and officer in default (imprisonment risk). Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.8(11). [Knowledge-based]

frequency_or_trigger: At registration; renewal every 5 years (10 years if income below Rs 5 crore in each of preceding 2 years, per Finance Act 2025 amendment)
obligation_register: Failure to obtain/renew 12A/12AB registration or 80G approval does not itself carry a monetary penalty, but the direct consequence is loss of income-tax exemption - the entity's income becomes taxable at the maximum marginal rate, and donors lose the 80G deduction. Liable: the trust/institution (loss of exemption), not a named officer. Basis: Income-tax Act 1961 ss.12A, 12AA/12AB, 80G(5). [Knowledge-based]

compliance_name: Charitable entity audit and return (Form 10B/10BB, ITR-7)
description: Audit report and ITR by charitable trusts
obligation_register: Failure to file the audit report (Form 10B/10BB) along with the return, or non-filing of ITR-7, results in denial of exemption under s.11/12 for that year and the income being taxed as that of a normal entity (also attracting s.234F late-fee and s.271B-type consequences where a compulsory audit under s.44AB is separately triggered). Liable: the trust/institution (loss of exemption); trustees/managing committee bear practical responsibility. Basis: Income-tax Act 1961 s.12A(1)(b). [Knowledge-based]

description: State Registrar filings for societies and public trusts
acts_rules: Societies Registration Act 1860 / State Public Trust Acts
verification: Needs manual check - varies by state
obligation_register: Non-filing of annual accounts/returns with the Registrar of Societies or Charity Commissioner is governed by the applicable state Societies Registration Act/Public Trusts Act, and typically results in show-cause notices, fines prescribed under the state Act/rules, and in serious cases removal of trustees or supersession of the managing committee; the exact penalty varies by state and was not independently verified for this register. Liable: trustees/governing body members responsible for filing. Basis: Societies Registration Act 1860 / applicable State Public Trusts Act - Penalty provision not independently confirmed - consult a company secretary/legal counsel. [Needs manual check]

compliance_name: FCRA registration, annual return (FC-4) and quarterly disclosure
description: Receive foreign contribution only with FCRA registration
frequency_or_trigger: Annual FC-4 by 31 Dec; quarterly receipt disclosure on website
obligation_register: Non-filing of FC-4/quarterly disclosures: penalty of Rs 1,00,000 or 5% of the foreign contribution received during the period of non-submission, whichever is greater; continued/serious violations empower the Central Government to suspend or cancel FCRA registration under s.13/14, barring re-registration for 3 years. Liable: the association/company (registration holder) and its office-bearers responsible for compliance. Basis: Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act 2010 s.37 (read with s.18, r.17 FCRR 2011). [Search-confirmed - harchandani.in, fmsfindia.org.in]

description: Deduct and deposit TDS by 7th of next month (30 April for March)
acts_rules: Income-tax Act 2025 (from 1 Apr 2026, tax year 2026-27 onwards; Chapter XIX-B/s.393-395); Income-tax Act 1961 Chapter XVII-B for pre-1 Apr 2026 periods
obligation_register: Failure to deduct/deposit TDS: interest under s.201(1A) at 1%/1.5% per month plus disallowance of the expense under s.40(a)(ia); genuine non-deduction (not mere late deposit) also attracts a penalty under s.271C equal to the tax not deducted, and prosecution under s.276B (imprisonment 3 months to 7 years plus fine) for failure to pay deducted tax to the Government. Liable: the deductor (company/principal officer as 'person responsible'). Basis: Income-tax Act 1961 ss.201(1A), 271C, 276B (Income-tax Act 2025 ss.393-395 for periods from 1 Apr 2026). [Search-confirmed - blog.tdsman.com, disytax.com]

Late/non-filing of the quarterly TDS return: late fee under s.234E of Rs 200 per day (capped at the TDS amount), plus penalty under s.271H of Rs 10,000 to Rs 1,00,000 for continued default or incorrect particulars. Liable: the deductor (company/principal officer). Basis: Income-tax Act 1961 ss.234E, 271H. [Knowledge-based]

frequency_or_trigger: Form 16 by 15 June; 16A within 15 days of quarterly due date
form_or_filing: Form 130/131 (tax year 2026-27 onwards, s.395 IT Act 2025); Form 16/16A for pre-1 Apr 2026 periods
obligation_register: Failure to issue TDS certificates (Form 16/16A) within the prescribed time: penalty under s.272A(2)(g) of Rs 100 per day of default, subject to the amount of tax deductible. Liable: the deductor (company/principal officer). Basis: Income-tax Act 1961 s.272A(2)(g). [Knowledge-based]

Failure to collect/deposit TCS: interest under s.206C(7) at 1% per month on the amount not deposited; failure to collect attracts penalty under s.271CA equal to the tax not collected, and prosecution under s.276BB for failure to pay collected tax. Liable: the collector (company/principal officer). Basis: Income-tax Act 1961 ss.206C(7), 271CA, 276BB. [Search-confirmed - callmyca.com, ebizfiling.com]

Shortfall/default in advance-tax payment: interest under s.234B (1% per month for shortfall of 90% of assessed tax) and s.234C (1% per month for deferment of instalments); no separate penal fine applies, but interest is mandatory and compounds the tax liability. Liable: the company (assessee) itself. Basis: Income-tax Act 1961 ss.234B, 234C. [Knowledge-based]

frequency_or_trigger: 31 July non-audit; 31 October audit cases; 30 Nov for TP cases (as amended)
obligation_register: Late filing of ITR: late fee under s.234F of Rs 1,000 (income up to Rs 5 lakh) or Rs 5,000 (filed by 31 Dec of the assessment year)/Rs 10,000 (filed after); non-filing can also attract prosecution under s.276CC in serious cases. Liable: the company (assessee); principal officer is the person responsible for filing. Basis: Income-tax Act 1961 s.234F (s.276CC for wilful non-filing). [Search-confirmed - learn.quicko.com, sahi.com]

description: Tax audit where turnover exceeds limits
obligation_register: Failure to get accounts audited/furnish the tax-audit report (3CA/3CB-3CD) by the due date: penalty equal to 0.5% of total sales/turnover/gross receipts, subject to a maximum of Rs 1,50,000, unless reasonable cause under s.273B is shown. Liable: the company (assessee); signing partner/director bears practical responsibility. Basis: Income-tax Act 1961 s.271B. [Search-confirmed - taxbuddy.com, taxgarden.in]

description: Accountant's report on international/specified domestic transactions
obligation_register: Failure to furnish the transfer-pricing report (Form 3CEB): penalty of Rs 1,00,000, separate from and in addition to transfer-pricing adjustment penalties under s.270A/271AA. Liable: the company (assessee). Basis: Income-tax Act 1961 s.271BA. [Search-confirmed - disytax.com, taxupdate.in]

description: Master file and country-by-country reporting for groups above thresholds
obligation_register: Failure to maintain/furnish the master file (3CEAA) or CbCR (3CEAB): penalty under s.271AA of Rs 5,00,000 for master-file default, and under s.271GB a graded penalty of Rs 5,000-15,000 per day (and up to Rs 50,000 per day for continuing default) for CbCR non-compliance. Liable: the company (assessee)/constituent entity. Basis: Income-tax Act 1961 ss.271AA, 271GB. [Knowledge-based]

description: Remittance to non-residents certificate and information
obligation_register: Failure to furnish/incorrect furnishing of Form 15CA/15CB information for foreign remittances: penalty of Rs 1,00,000 for each default under s.271-I. Liable: the remitter (company)/authorised signatory. Basis: Income-tax Act 1961 s.271-I (read with s.195, r.37BB). [Search-confirmed - taxguru.in, xflowpay.com]

Failure to apply for or quote PAN/TAN, or quoting an incorrect PAN/TAN: penalty of Rs 10,000 for each default under s.272B (PAN) and a parallel penalty under s.272BB for TAN defaults. Liable: the company/person responsible for the transaction or deduction. Basis: Income-tax Act 1961 ss.272B, 272BB (obligations under ss.139A, 203A). [Search-confirmed - taxguru.in, incometaxindia.gov.in]

description: Equalisation levy on specified digital services
form_or_filing: Not applicable - levy discontinued (Form 1 relevant only for pre-abolition periods)
acts_rules: Finance Act 2016 Chapter VIII (Equalisation Levy) - abolished: 2% e-commerce levy withdrawn from 1 Aug 2024; 6% levy on online advertisements withdrawn from 1 Apr 2025
obligation_register: The equalisation levy (2% e-commerce levy and 6% online-advertisement levy) has been withdrawn (2% levy from 1 Aug 2024, 6% levy from 1 Apr 2025); for periods when the levy applied, failure to deduct/deposit attracted interest under s.170 and penalty under s.171 of the Finance Act 2016 (penalty equal to the levy amount for non-deduction, or Rs 1,000/day up to the levy amount for non-payment of a deducted levy); no fresh liability arises for post-withdrawal periods. Liable (for legacy periods): the payer who failed to deduct/deposit the levy. Basis: Finance Act 2016 ss.170-171 (Chapter VIII) - now withdrawn prospectively. [Knowledge-based]

Failure to file Form 61A (SFT) by the due date: penalty of Rs 500 per day of default until service of notice, and Rs 1,000 per day thereafter if still not filed; furnishing inaccurate information attracts a separate penalty of Rs 50,000 under s.271FAA. Liable: the reporting entity (company). Basis: Income-tax Act 1961 s.271FA (s.271FAA for inaccurate SFT). [Search-confirmed - cleartax.in, tax2win.in]

Non-response/non-compliance with income-tax e-proceedings notices (e.g. under ss.142(1), 143(2)): penalty under s.272A(1) of Rs 10,000 for each default/failure, in addition to any best-judgment assessment consequences under s.144. Liable: the company (assessee)/principal officer responding to the notice. Basis: Income-tax Act 1961 s.272A(1). [Knowledge-based]

Failure to obtain GST registration when liable: penalty equal to the tax evaded or Rs 10,000, whichever is higher, under s.122(1); the person also remains liable for the unpaid tax with interest under s.50 and may face prosecution under s.132 for large-scale evasion. Liable: the person/company liable to register. Basis: CGST Act 2017 s.122(1) (read with ss.22, 24). [Knowledge-based]

Late filing of GSTR-1: late fee under s.47 of Rs 50 per day (Rs 25 CGST + Rs 25 SGST), or Rs 20 per day (Rs 10+Rs 10) for nil returns, subject to notified caps; persistent default also blocks e-way bill generation and GSTR-3B filing. Liable: the registered person (company). Basis: CGST Act 2017 s.47. [Search-confirmed - tallysolutions.com, cleartax.in]

Late filing of GSTR-3B: late fee under s.47 of Rs 50 per day (Rs 20 for nil returns), subject to notified caps, plus interest under s.50 at 18% p.a. on the tax paid late. Liable: the registered person (company). Basis: CGST Act 2017 s.47, s.50. [Search-confirmed - tallysolutions.com, cleartax.in]

Late filing of GSTR-9 (annual return): late fee under s.47(2) of Rs 200 per day (Rs 100 CGST + Rs 100 SGST), subject to a cap of 0.25% of turnover in the State/UT under each Act. Liable: the registered person (company). Basis: CGST Act 2017 s.47(2). [Knowledge-based]

description: Self-certified reconciliation where AATO exceeds Rs5 crore
obligation_register: Since GSTR-9C is filed together with/following GSTR-9, its late filing attracts the same late fee as GSTR-9 under s.47(2) - Rs 200 per day (Rs 100 CGST + Rs 100 SGST), capped at 0.25% of turnover in the State/UT under each Act. Liable: the registered person (company). Basis: CGST Act 2017 s.44/s.47(2). [Knowledge-based]

description: Generate IRN for B2B where AATO threshold met
frequency_or_trigger: Per invoice; report within 30 days for AATO Rs10cr+
verification: Search-confirmed - gst e-invoice guides (xflowpay.com, tallysolutions.com) - threshold Rs 5 crore AATO; verify against CBIC notification
obligation_register: Failure to issue a valid e-invoice/obtain an IRN where mandated: the invoice is treated as not having been issued at all, attracting the general invoicing penalty under s.122(1)(i) (Rs 10,000 or the tax evaded, whichever is higher) and denial of ITC to the recipient; goods may also be detained in transit under s.129 for lack of a valid tax invoice. Liable: the supplier (company). Basis: CGST Act 2017 s.122(1)(i) (read with CGST Rules 2017 r.48). [Knowledge-based]

description: E-way bill for movement of goods above Rs50,000
obligation_register: Transporting goods without a valid e-way bill: penalty equal to 100% of the tax payable (or Rs 10,000, if higher) to release detained/seized goods, plus a per-kilometre penalty framework under s.129 for the distance travelled without a valid e-way bill; goods and the conveyance may be detained/seized until tax and penalty are paid. Liable: the person in charge of the conveyance / consignor (company). Basis: CGST Act 2017 s.129 (read with r.138). [Search-confirmed - taxbuddy.com, irisgst.com]

description: Details of goods sent to job workers
obligation_register: No bespoke fine is prescribed for late filing of ITC-04; default is enforced through the general penalty for contraventions where no separate penalty is specified - up to Rs 25,000 under s.125, in addition to potential denial/reversal of ITC on goods sent for job work not accounted for within the prescribed period. Liable: the principal manufacturer (company). Basis: CGST Act 2017 s.125 (read with r.45). [Knowledge-based]

Wrongly availing/utilising ITC beyond what is reflected in GSTR-2B: recovery of the excess ITC with interest under s.50, and penalty under s.73 (no fraud - up to 10% of tax or Rs 10,000, whichever higher) or s.74 (fraud/wilful misstatement - up to 100% of tax). Liable: the registered person (company) claiming the ITC. Basis: CGST Act 2017 s.16 read with ss.73/74. [Knowledge-based]

description: Pay tax under reverse charge and self-invoice
obligation_register: Failure to pay tax under reverse charge (RCM): the recipient remains liable for the unpaid tax with interest under s.50, and penalty under s.122(1)/s.73-74 as applicable (up to 10%/100% of the tax depending on whether fraud is involved). Liable: the recipient liable to pay tax under RCM (company). Basis: CGST Act 2017 s.9(3)/9(4) read with ss.50, 73-74, 122. [Knowledge-based]

description: TDS by notified deductors; TCS by e-commerce operators
obligation_register: Failure to deduct/collect or deposit GST TDS/TCS (GSTR-7/GSTR-8): interest under s.50 on the amount not deposited, late fee under s.47 for late filing of GSTR-7/8 (Rs 100/day, capped at Rs 5,000), and general penalty under s.122(1) equal to the tax involved or Rs 10,000, whichever is higher, for failure to deduct/collect. Liable: the deductor/e-commerce operator (company). Basis: CGST Act 2017 ss.51, 52 read with s.47, s.122. [Knowledge-based]

compliance_name: GST annual return for composition dealers (CMP-08, GSTR-4)
obligation_register: Late filing of CMP-08/GSTR-4 by a composition dealer: late fee under s.47 - Rs 200 per day (Rs 100 CGST + Rs 100 SGST) for GSTR-4, subject to notified caps/reduced rates for composition taxpayers, plus interest under s.50 on delayed tax payment. Liable: the composition taxpayer (company). Basis: CGST Act 2017 s.47 (read with s.10). [Knowledge-based]

Failure to claim/process a GST refund correctly does not itself attract a penalty on the claimant; however, if a refund is obtained by fraud or wilful misstatement it is recoverable with interest and a penalty equal to the amount of refund wrongly obtained under s.54(1) read with s.74. Liable: the claimant (company), only where the claim is fraudulent. Basis: CGST Act 2017 s.54 read with s.74. [Knowledge-based]

description: Letter of undertaking to export without IGST
frequency_or_trigger: Annual, before first export of FY
obligation_register: Failure to furnish LUT (or furnishing it but not exporting within time) requires the exporter to pay IGST on the export with interest under s.50 from the date of the invoice (no separate LUT-specific penalty is prescribed; the LUT itself is then treated as not furnished for future exports). Liable: the exporter (company). Basis: CGST Rules 2017 r.96A. [Knowledge-based]

Failure to apply for amendment/cancellation of GST registration where required, or continuing to file returns without cancelling a defunct registration, attracts the general penalty under s.125 (up to Rs 25,000) for contravention where no specific penalty is prescribed; suo-motu cancellation by the proper officer can also follow under s.29(2). Liable: the registered person (company). Basis: CGST Act 2017 s.125 (read with ss.28-29). [Knowledge-based]

description: Input service distributor registration and returns
obligation_register: Failure to accept/reject invoices in the Invoice Management System (IMS) or non-compliance by an ISD in distributing ITC is enforced through the general penalty under s.125 (up to Rs 25,000), in addition to ITC mismatches being disallowed/reversed. Liable: the registered person/ISD (company). Basis: CGST Act 2017 s.125 (read with s.20). [Knowledge-based]

Non-response to a scrutiny notice (ASMT-10) leads to best-judgment assessment and demand proceedings under s.73 (no fraud - tax plus interest plus penalty up to 10% of tax or Rs 10,000, whichever higher) or s.74 (fraud/wilful misstatement - tax plus interest plus penalty up to 100% of tax). Liable: the registered person (company). Basis: CGST Act 2017 ss.61, 73, 74. [Knowledge-based]

description: Register and pay provident fund contributions
acts_rules: Code on Social Security, 2020 (in force 21 Nov 2025; erstwhile Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 subsumed); EPF Scheme 1952
obligation_register: Deducting employees' PF contribution and failing to deposit it, or otherwise defaulting on EPF contribution: imprisonment of 1 to 3 years and fine up to Rs 1,00,000 for the first default on deducted-but-undeposited contributions, rising to imprisonment of 2 to 5 years and a fine of Rs 3,00,000 for subsequent defaults; the Code also allows compounding for many violations and mandates a 30-day improvement notice before prosecution. Liable: the employer/person responsible for management of the establishment (e.g. director/occupier). Basis: Code on Social Security 2020 s.133 (erstwhile EPF & MP Act 1952 s.14). [Search-confirmed - greythr.com, ksandk.com]

compliance_name: EPF annual return / UAN and ELI
form_or_filing: Form 3A/6A (subsumed by ECR) [legacy form name; Code-era format to confirm]
acts_rules: Code on Social Security, 2020 (in force 21 Nov 2025; erstwhile Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 subsumed)
obligation_register: Default in filing the EPF annual return or updating UAN/ELI details is enforced through the same employer-default penalty regime as monthly contributions - imprisonment (1-3 years, extending to 2-5 years for repeat defaults) and fine (up to Rs 1,00,000/Rs 3,00,000), subject to the Code's compounding and improvement-notice safeguards. Liable: the employer/person responsible for management of the establishment. Basis: Code on Social Security 2020 s.133 (erstwhile EPF & MP Act 1952 s.14). [Search-confirmed - greythr.com, ksandk.com]

acts_rules: Code on Social Security, 2020 (in force 21 Nov 2025; erstwhile Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948 subsumed)
obligation_register: Failure to pay ESI contributions (including deducted employee share): minimum imprisonment of 1 year and fine of not less than Rs 10,000 where the employee's contribution was deducted but not paid; other defaults punishable with imprisonment up to 1 year or fine up to Rs 4,000; continuing post-conviction default attracts a further fine of up to Rs 1,000 per day. Liable: the employer (principal employer/person responsible for the establishment). Basis: ESI Act 1948 s.85 (as continued/aligned under the Code on Social Security 2020). [Search-confirmed - taxguru.in, indiankanoon.org]

form_or_filing: Form 6 [legacy form name; Code-era format to confirm]
acts_rules: Code on Social Security, 2020 (in force 21 Nov 2025; erstwhile Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948 subsumed)
obligation_register: Failure to file the ESI half-yearly return is enforced through the same employer-default penalty regime as contribution defaults under s.85 - imprisonment up to 1 year (minimum 1 year where deducted contribution is involved) or fine up to Rs 4,000/Rs 10,000 as applicable, plus recovery of damages by the Corporation. Liable: the employer (principal employer/person responsible). Basis: ESI Act 1948 s.85. [Search-confirmed - taxguru.in, indiankanoon.org]

form_or_filing: Form F nomination; Form I [legacy form name; Code-era format to confirm]
acts_rules: Code on Social Security, 2020 (in force 21 Nov 2025; erstwhile Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 subsumed)
obligation_register: Default in payment of gratuity or contravention of the Act's provisions: imprisonment of not less than 3 months up to 1 year, or fine of Rs 10,000 to Rs 20,000, or both; where the default relates specifically to non-payment of gratuity due, imprisonment of not less than 6 months up to 2 years. Liable: the employer. Basis: Payment of Gratuity Act 1972 s.9(2) (continued under Code on Social Security 2020 s.135). [Search-confirmed - indiankanoon.org, ssrana.in]

description: Bonus payment and Form D annual return

acts_rules: Code on Wages, 2019 (in force 21 Nov 2025; erstwhile Payment of Bonus Act, 1965 subsumed)
obligation_register: Contravention of the Payment of Bonus Act provisions, or failure to comply with a direction/requisition under the Act: imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to Rs 1,000, or both. Liable: the employer/person responsible. Basis: Payment of Bonus Act 1965 s.28 (continued under Code on Wages 2019 s.54, which prescribes enhanced fines up to Rs 50,000/imprisonment for repeat default). [Search-confirmed - indiankanoon.org, indiacode.nic.in]

Non-registration/non-renewal under the State Shops and Establishments Act typically attracts a fine prescribed by the specific state Act/rules (commonly in the range of a few hundred to a few thousand rupees, with a further daily fine for continuing default, varying by state); the exact amount depends on the state where the establishment is located and was not independently verified for this register. Liable: the employer/occupier of the establishment. Basis: applicable State Shops and Establishments Act - Penalty provision not independently confirmed - consult a company secretary/legal counsel. [Needs manual check]

description: Register and pay PT in states that levy it
acts_rules: State Professional Tax Acts (e.g., Maharashtra, Karnataka, WB, TN)
obligation_register: Non-payment/non-registration for Professional Tax attracts a penalty and interest prescribed by the specific State Professional Tax Act/rules (commonly a percentage per month of interest plus a penalty for late registration/payment, e.g. under the Maharashtra, Karnataka, WB and TN Acts), with the exact quantum varying by state and not independently verified for this register. Liable: the employer (company) as the person responsible for deduction/payment. Basis: applicable State Professional Tax Act - Penalty provision not independently confirmed - consult a company secretary/legal counsel. [Needs manual check]

Failure to obtain the employer's Professional Tax Enrolment Certificate (PTEC) or delay in payment attracts a state-specific penalty/interest (e.g. a percentage of the tax due per month of delay plus a late-registration penalty), with the exact quantum varying by state and not independently verified for this register. Liable: the employer (company). Basis: applicable State Professional Tax Act (PTEC provisions) - Penalty provision not independently confirmed - consult a company secretary/legal counsel. [Needs manual check]

acts_rules: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act 2013
obligation_register: Non-constitution of the Internal Committee (or absence of a POSH policy/training): fine up to Rs 50,000 for the first contravention; on a second or subsequent contravention the fine is doubled and repeated non-compliance can lead to cancellation/withdrawal of the business licence or registration required for carrying on business. Liable: the employer (company). Basis: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act 2013 s.26. [Search-confirmed - apnilaw.com, petpooja.com]

Failure to conduct mandatory POSH awareness/training programmes or display the required notice is treated as a contravention of the Act's employer obligations under s.19, carrying the same penalty as other POSH non-compliance - fine up to Rs 50,000 for the first offence, doubling on repetition, with risk of licence/registration cancellation for continued default. Liable: the employer (company). Basis: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act 2013 s.26 (read with s.19). [Search-confirmed - apnilaw.com, petpooja.com]

description: No child labour in hazardous work
